regimens.indication: Preventive Treatment of Migraine — Adults (Standard Dose)

refs.quote: AIMOVIG is indicated for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults.
The recommended dosage of AIMOVIG is 70 mg injected subcutaneously once monthly.

regimens.dose_text: 70 mg injected subcutaneously once monthly into the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm. Allow to sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes prior to administration. If a dose is missed, administer as soon as possible and schedule monthly from the date of the last dose. In geriatric patients, start at the low end (70 mg).

tier.note: No adequate human pregnancy data are available; monkey studies at ~20x human exposure showed no adverse offspring effects.

refs.quote: There are no adequate data on the developmental risk associated with the use of AIMOVIG in pregnant women. No adverse effects on offspring were observed when pregnant monkeys were administered erenumab-aooe throughout gestation

contraception.value: No interaction with combined oral contraceptives; discontinue erenumab (~28-day half-life) at least 5 to 6 months prior to planned conception per AHS headache guidelines.

refs.quote: Erenumab is an IgG2 anti-CGRP receptor monoclonal antibody (~28-day half-life) with no interaction with combined oral contraceptives; AHS headache guidelines recommend discontinuing erenumab at least 5 to 6 months prior to planned conception. Rimegepant Contraception & Washout: Rimegepant does not reduce ethinylestradiol or norelgestromin

pregnancy_pk.value: IgG2 monoclonal antibody with increasing transplacental transfer via FcRn during the 2nd and 3rd trimesters; human data are limited and CGRP blockade raises theoretical concern for gestational hypertension.

refs.quote: Erenumab is an IgG2 monoclonal antibody that crosses the placenta increasingly via FcRn during the second and third trimesters; human pregnancy registry data remain limited and theoretical CGRP blockade raises concern for gestational hypertension or impaired uteroplacental vasodilation. refs.quote: Although clinical milk data for erenumab are limited, large monoclonal antibodies transfer poorly into mature breast milk and undergo gastrointestinal degradation; use caution while nursing newborns or preterm infants and monitor feeding and growth.
